keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Khadga page dates the dynasty from 625 (Khadgodyama 625-640, Jatakhadga 640-658) but Cliopatria's row begins in 656. The 656 outline is reused for 625-636 as a dependency of Gauda: the Shashanka page says his 'domain stretched from Vanga to Bhuvanesha' until his death in 636 and the Samatata page's infobox has '6th century-7th century: Gauda Kingdom', so the same cells cannot also be an independent state in those years (repair of the review finding; the gauda-kingdom keyframe 612-637 holds the Bangladesh cells). The Samatata page says the Khadgas 'were originally from Vanga but later conquered Samatata' without a date, so the early core may have been smaller; no page opened gives it. Cliopatria area 90,427 km2 (294 grid cells); neither page gives an area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the full 656 outline, drawn as the Khadgas' own land from 637, the year the Gauda dossier ends the kingdom (Shashanka d. 636, 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harsha and Bhaskaravarman'). harsha-s-empire no longer draws these cells (its 637 gain and 637-646 keyframes now subtract the 656 outline), so the Bengal core is claimed once in 637-655.

90,427 km2 (Dhaka, Khulna, Chittagong, Barisal, Tripura and a corner of West Bengal) against the Khadga page's 'Vanga and Samatata' and the Samatata page's districts 'Sylhet, Dhaka, Comilla, Noakhali, Barisal, Khulna and parts of Tripura, Chittagong'. region.text: 'the areas of Vanga and Samatata in ancient Bengal', south-east Bengal around Karmanta Vasaka (Comilla), drawn as Cliopatria's Khadga outline

ledger.note: 625: Khadgodyama founds the Khadga dynasty in Vanga and Samatata. Infobox 'Established 625 CE'; 'ruled the areas of Vanga and Samatata in ancient Bengal from 625 CE to 716 CE'. The Samatata page says they 'were originally from Vanga but later conquered Samatata' (undated) and the Khadga page says the dynasty rose after the fall of Gauda, which the Gauda page puts at 636/637. Review repair: from 625 to 636 the outline is a Gauda dependency (next event), not independent land.

625-636: the Khadga outline as a Gauda dependency (the researcher's reading). Two pages disagree: the Khadga infobox says 'Established: 625 CE' and the text says the dynasty 'emerged as a powerful kingdom of Bengal between the fall of Gauda Kingdom and the rise of the Pala Empire'; the Shashanka page says his 'domain stretched from Vanga to Bhuvanesha' and 'Historians place his rule between 600 and 636'; the Samatata page has '6th century-7th century: Gauda Kingdom'. No page calls the Khadgas Gauda's vassals, and the Khadga page says they retained sovereignty over Vanga; the dependency is only the reading that keeps all the dates and stops two dossiers drawing the same cells. Mirror events for gauda-kingdom: vassal_start 625 and vassal_end 637 with counterpart khadga-dynasty, and a trim of its 612-637 keyframe by this outline.

region.text: Vanga and Samatata, the Khadga outline under Gauda's overlordship until Shashanka's death in 636

ledger.note: 637: the Khadgas are independent. Shashanka died in 636 and his son Manava 'ruled the kingdom for eight months'; 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harsha and Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa' (Shashanka page), and the gauda-kingdom dossier ends the kingdom in 637. The Khadga page says the dynasty emerged 'between the fall of Gauda Kingdom and the rise of the Pala Empire' and gives no year for its independence, so 637 is the Gauda dossier's year for the fall (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 716: the Khadga dynasty ends and the Deva dynasty takes Vanga and Samatata. Infobox 'disestablished 716 CE'; the last listed ruler is Balabhatta (707-716), then Udirnakhadga with no reign given.

certainty.note: The pages name regions (Vanga, Samatata, 'trans-Meghna territories') and districts, never a line; the delta's rivers shift and no treaty or survey fixes a frontier.

notes:
Two pages only (budget 1-2) plus the Gauda page opened for harsha-s-empire. Neither Khadga page mentions Harsha, Kamarupa, Tibet or the Palas' arrival with a date; no contest, vassalage or war is therefore recorded.
Cliopatria rows to correct: the row (656-704) starts 31 years after the page's 625 and ends 12 years before 716; Cliopatria draws Bengal as Harsha's Empire for 612-655 (see harsha-s-empire notes) and has no shape for 705-749 until the Pala Empire. The 625-655 and 705-716 keyframes reuse the 656 and 692 outlines (confidence 2 at best).
Disagreement: the Khadga infobox says 625, the text says the dynasty rose after Gauda fell (Gauda page: 636/637); the Samatata page says only '7th century-8th century' for Khadgas and Bhadras and gives no date. The infobox dates are used and the discrepancy is in the found note.
States needing dossiers: Bhadra dynasty (predecessor in Samatata), First Deva dynasty (successor, 8th-9th century). Udirnakhadga (reign '716-?') is not in the ruler strip. Karmanta Vasaka's coordinates are Comilla's, the nearest gazetteer place to Barakamata. No gazetteer names are missing (Bengal, Cliopatria shapes).
Repair of 2026-10-19 (review finding on the 625-655 keyframe): I chose the reviewer's option (a). The 625-636 outline is a Gauda dependency: ledger vassal_start 625 and vassal_end 637 (counterpart gauda-kingdom, confidence 1), keyframe split at 637 (khadga-dynasty_625 for 625-636, khadga-dynasty_637 for 637-655, same 656 outline). Reason: the Shashanka page puts Vanga inside Shashanka's domain until 636 and the Samatata page's infobox lists '6th century-7th century: Gauda Kingdom', against the Khadga infobox's 625; a dependency keeps every date. Against it: the Khadga page says the dynasty retained sovereignty over Vanga and 'did not assume imperial titles', and no page says vassal, so confidence is 1; the colour agent may drop the tint. Option (b) (trim gauda-kingdom's keyframe and treat the Khadgas as independent from 625) is the fallback and needs the same gauda-kingdom trim.
Routed to gauda-kingdom's author (not edited here): (1) vassal_start 625 and vassal_end 637 with counterpart khadga-dynasty, region the Khadga 656 outline; (2) its keyframe gauda-kingdom_612 (612-637) and its 602/554 keyframes minus the Khadga outline from 625; (3) khadga-dynasty among its successors for Vanga and Samatata (its dissolve 637). harsha-s-empire now subtracts the Khadga outline from its 637 gain and its 637-646 keyframes, so Harsha no longer claims the land.
Disagreement with the reviewer: none.
